Received Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

SPECIMEN TYPE: Peripheral blood

TEST PERFORMED: DNA Extraction and Storage

METHODOLOGY:
Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood using standard column-based purification methods. DNA concentration and purity were assessed by spectrophotometry (NanoDrop) and fluorometry (Qubit). DNA integrity was evaluated by agarose gel electrophoresis.

RESULTS:

DNA EXTRACTION STATUS: Complete
DNA Concentration: 12.3 ng/μL (Reference range: >50 ng/μL)
A260/A280 Ratio: 1.65 (Reference range: 1.8-2.0)
A260/A230 Ratio: 0.89 (Reference range: 2.0-2.2)
Total Yield: 369 ng (Reference range: >1500 ng)

QUALITY ASSESSMENT: SUBOPTIMAL

The extracted DNA shows evidence of degradation with significant low molecular weight fragments observed on gel electrophoresis. The low concentration and poor purity ratios indicate potential contamination and/or inadequate cellular material in the original specimen.

STORAGE: DNA has been aliquoted and stored at -80°C in the Molecular Genetics Laboratory biobank.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS:
The suboptimal DNA quality may impose limitations on downstream molecular testing. Tests requiring high molecular weight DNA or large amounts of input material may not be feasible with this specimen. PCR-based assays targeting short amplicons may still be possible.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
1. Please consult with the laboratory regarding feasibility of specific molecular tests prior to ordering
2. Consider collection of a fresh specimen if high-quality DNA is required
3. Note: Karyotype analysis results are pending from the Cytogenetics Laboratory
